correctness.rationale: Exact incidence-graph correspondence, two-sided domination test, cycle/leaf removability, and biconditional tree classification prove the theorem for every m,n>=2. Weighted bipartite Prüfer identity with the surjection count yields precisely the two nonoverlapping Stirling sums. Separate direct vertex-subset enumeration checked 1,413,959 subsets across nine board shapes; computation is supporting evidence, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct published-finding corpus searches for rook minimal connected domination, complete-bipartite connected edge domination, Stirling formulas and bipartite tree leaves found no matching theorem. Accessible arXiv and ESA primary-text comparisons distinguish a general enumeration algorithm and an ordinary rook domination polynomial from the exact size distribution of inclusion-minimal connected sets. Existing OEIS all-connected counts cannot imply the size-by-size minimal spectrum without additional structural information. Novelty is assessed under remaining bibliographic risk, not certified uniqueness.
residual_risks: Nonindexed or differently phrased connected-edge-domination and bipartite line-graph enumerations may exist.
The bipartite Prüfer weighted enumerator itself is standard prior mathematics, not novel here.
Finite test cases do not validate novelty or infinite theorem by themselves.
No external independent mathematical review was undertaken.

value.rationale: Complete cardinality distribution of inclusion-minimal connected dominating sets for all rectangles is a natural exact structural classification. It distinguishes minimum and upper connected domination, determines their optimizer multiplicities, and proves arbitrarily long forbidden internal size intervals when n>=2m; these properties are not routine readings of the ordinary rook domination polynomial.
